comparisons.peer_topic: Lessee Accounting Policy for Operating Leases
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation records right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for substantially all operating leases on the Consolidated Balance Sheet at commencement, excluding short-term leases under the 12-month election. Right-of-use assets are reported in other assets, lease liabilities in accrued expenses and other liabilities, and lease expense is recognized on a straight-line basis in occupancy and equipment expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC recognize right-of-use (ROU) assets and lease liabilities for operating leases. However, they differ in lease term thresholds and initial measurement adjustments. GS applies the policy to leases 'longer than one year' and initially measures the ROU asset based on the lease liability adjusted for 'initial direct costs, lease incentives and amounts paid at or prior to lease commencement.' BAC excludes short-term leases with an 'initial term less than 12 months' and measures the ROU asset as the lease liability adjusted for 'any lease payments made prior to lease commencement and for any lease incentives,' without explicitly mentioning initial direct costs in the provided text. Both report these items in 'other assets' and 'other liabilities/accrued expenses'.

sentences.text: For leases longer than one year, the firm recognizes a right-of-use asset representing the right to use the underlying asset for the lease term, and a lease liability representing the liability to make payments.

An operating lease right-of-use asset is initially determined based on the operating lease liability, adjusted for initial direct costs, lease incentives and amounts paid at or prior to lease commencement.
Right-of-use assets are reported in other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheet, and the related lease liabilities are reported in accrued expenses and other liabilities.
All leases are recorded on the Consolidated Balance Sheet except leases with an initial term less than 12 months for which the Corporation made the short-term lease election.
Right-of-use assets initially equal the lease liability, adjusted for any lease payments made prior to lease commencement and for any lease incentives.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi recognizes lease liabilities and right-of-use (ROU) assets upon lease commencement based on the present value of lease payments discounted at the incremental borrowing rate, with ROU assets adjusted for pre-commencement payments and incentives. These assets and liabilities are included in Premises and equipment and Other liabilities, respectively, and are remeasured for certain modifications or when renewal/extension options become reasonably certain.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi recognize lease liabilities and ROU assets upon lease commencement for operating leases. A key similarity is the exclusion of renewal/extension options from the lease term unless the company is 'reasonably certain' to exercise them (Citi) or incorporates an 'assessment of the likelihood' (GS). However, they differ in the discount rate used for measurement: Citi uses the 'incremental borrowing rate,' whereas the provided GS text does not specify the discount rate used for the lease liability calculation. Both also adjust the initial ROU asset for pre-commencement payments and incentives.

sentences.text: For leases longer than one year, the firm recognizes a right-of-use asset representing the right to use the underlying asset for the lease term, and a lease liability representing the liability to make payments.
For leases where the firm has the option to terminate or extend the lease, an assessment of the likelihood of exercising the option is incorporated into the determination of the lease term.

An operating lease right-of-use asset is initially determined based on the operating lease liability, adjusted for initial direct costs, lease incentives and amounts paid at or prior to lease commencement.

Lease liabilities and right-of-use (ROU) assets are recognized when Citi enters into these leases and represent Citi's obligations and rights to use these assets over the period of the leases, and may be remeasured for certain modifications.

These leases may contain renewal and extension options and early termination features; however, these options do not impact the lease term unless the Company is reasonably certain that it will exercise the options.
At lease commencement, lease liabilities are recognized based on the present value of the remaining lease payments and discounted using the Company's incremental borrowing rate.
ROU assets initially equal the lease liability, adjusted for any lease payments made prior to lease commencement and for any lease incentives.

comparisons.peer_topic: Lease Liability Recognition and Measurement Policy
comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorganChase recognizes operating lease liabilities and corresponding right-of-use assets at the lease commencement date based on the present value of future minimum lease payments, discounted using the Firm's collateralized borrowing rate. Lease terms generally include options to extend or terminate if reasonably certain to be exercised, and terms are 20 years or less, with all leases over twelve months reported on the balance sheet.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorganChase recognize operating lease liabilities and corresponding ROU assets at lease commencement. Both firms determine the lease term based on contractual maturity and include extension/termination options if 'reasonably certain' to be exercised. They differ in the discount rate: JPM explicitly states it uses the 'collateralized borrowing rate,' while GS does not specify the rate in the provided text. Additionally, JPM explicitly states that the ROU asset includes 'initial direct costs incurred,' whereas GS also adjusts for 'initial direct costs' but the provided sentence structure differs slightly in grouping.

sentences.text: For leases longer than one year, the firm recognizes a right-of-use asset representing the right to use the underlying asset for the lease term, and a lease liability representing the liability to make payments.
For leases where the firm has the option to terminate or extend the lease, an assessment of the likelihood of exercising the option is incorporated into the determination of the lease term.

An operating lease right-of-use asset is initially determined based on the operating lease liability, adjusted for initial direct costs, lease incentives and amounts paid at or prior to lease commencement.

These leases generally have terms of 20 years or less, determined based on the contractual maturity of the lease, and include periods covered by options to extend or terminate the lease when the Firm is reasonably certain that it will exercise those options.
All leases with lease terms greater than twelve months are reported as a lease liability with a corresponding right-of-use ("ROU") asset.
Operating lease liabilities and ROU assets are recognized at the lease commencement date based on the present value of the future minimum lease payments over the lease term.

The future lease payments are discounted at a rate that estimates the Firm's collateralized borrowing rate for financing instruments of a similar term and are included in accounts payable and other liabilities.
The operating lease ROU assets, predominantly included in premises and equipment, also include any lease prepayments made, plus initial direct costs incurred, less any lease incentives received.
